inspection_summary: Inspected all 887 normalized lines. Lines 1-38 are the tail and references of a different preceding article; the assigned Heath-Brown article runs from its journal/title matter at lines 40-48 through the proof ending at line 855, followed by references. The checked prose supports a rich chain from pair correlation through weighted zero exponential sums and smoothed prime-counting variance to prime-gap consequences. sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Introduces explicit-formula and smoothing machinery; Lemma 2 reduces a mean-square short-interval prime-counting deviation to a weighted zero sum plus controlled sieve/error terms.

sections_inspected.label: Preparations: pair correlation to exponential sums
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Lemmas 3 and 4 convert pair correlation into an exact weighted L2 identity and then a pointwise bound for zero exponential sums.

sections_inspected.label: Proof of Theorem 1
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses the explicit-formula bridge and the exponential-sum bound to turn decay of pair correlation into the stated prime-number-theorem error.

sections_inspected.label: Proof of Theorem 2
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Encodes large prime gaps in a nonnegative short-interval variance and bounds the resulting low- and high-zero-frequency ranges by local maxima of pair correlation.

sections_inspected.label: Preparations for Theorem 3
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Evaluates a weighted zero-sum energy in terms of pair correlation, controls tails, and derives the kernel identity collected as Lemma 5.

sections_inspected.label: Completion of Theorem 3
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Combines prime variance with the pair-correlation kernel, averages a scale parameter to localize the usable range, and uses diagonal/off-diagonal positivity plus sieve tail bounds to force a close pair of primes.

accepted_units.title: Montgomery pair correlation as a source of prime-distribution information
accepted_units.why_material: Introduces the weighted pair-correlation statistic, distinguishes the proved restricted asymptotic from the broader conjecture, and identifies consequences for zero simplicity, establishing the zero-statistics side of the transfer problem.
accepted_units.context_note: Carried unchanged from v1 and coherent as an introductory unit.

accepted_units.title: From localized pair correlation to an actual close pair of primes
accepted_units.why_material: Provides the full final transfer architecture: combine the prime variance and pair-correlation energy identities, localize by averaging, separate diagonal from off-diagonal contributions, discard remote prime ranges with a sieve bound, and infer existence from positivity.
accepted_units.context_note: Carried unchanged from v1. Its opening invokes Lemmas 2 and 5, whose mechanisms and admissible ranges occur at lines 212-308 and 571-676 and are needed to interpret the proof without reconstruction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Substantial formula and kernel dependence with recurring OCR corruption; the strategic sequence is prose-supported, but constants and exact inequalities require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Why zero statistics should improve classical prime-gap bounds
accepted_units.why_material: Contrasts classical RH bounds and short-interval results with Gallagher-Mueller and Mueller hypotheses, then frames the paper's task as weakening or sharpening the pair-correlation assumptions needed for prime consequences.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the missing bridge between the pair-correlation introduction and the theorem package.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Named-result relations and qualitative improvements are prose-readable; the displayed exact estimates are OCR-sensitive and should be checked against the scan before numerical use.

accepted_units.title: Reduce short-interval prime variance to a weighted zero sum
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 2 supplies the reusable analytic reduction on the prime side: smooth a short increment, insert the explicit-formula decomposition, split the error contributions, and control prime-pair terms by a uniform sieve estimate and remaining terms by mean-square bounds.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof's Cauchy-Schwarz split and sieve input are readable in prose, although the displayed definition and bound are degraded. Lemma 1 at lines 202-210 is deliberately not promoted as a unit because its exact formula is unsafe in this OCR.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High; the semantic reduction is recoverable, but the precise smoothing function, powers, and error expression require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Pair correlation as weighted L2 energy of a zero exponential sum
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 3 makes the central representation change exact: the pair-correlation weight is the Fourier transform of a positive kernel, so the two-zero statistic equals an integrated squared exponential sum.
accepted_units.context_note: The prose explicitly states that the identity is independent of RH and even of the ordinates being zeta zeros, revealing a reusable harmonic-analytic mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The transform identity and symbols are formula-dependent but short and structurally recoverable; scan verification is needed for exact normalization.

accepted_units.title: Control a pointwise zero sum by nearby pair-correlation energy
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 4 combines a one-dimensional smoothing inequality, partial summation, and the positive-kernel identity to bound a pointwise exponential sum by a local maximum of pair correlation.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the bridge that allows an averaged pair statistic to control the explicit-formula term used in Theorem 1.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate-to-high formula dependency; the bounding strategy is prose-readable, while exact powers and integration limits require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Pair-correlation decay implies a sharper prime-counting error
accepted_units.why_material: Shows a clean transfer pattern: truncate the explicit formula at two scales, use the hypothesis and Lemma 4 on the long range, use a trivial bound on the short range, then choose the scale after fixing the target error.
accepted_units.context_note: The epsilon-then-scale choice exposes the quantifier order behind the little-o conclusion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The logical sequence is reliable from prose; exact displayed exponents and normalization remain OCR-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Encode large prime gaps inside short-interval variance
accepted_units.why_material: Turns each sufficiently large consecutive-prime gap into a region where the short-interval counting error is forced, sums those nonnegative contributions, and invokes Lemma 2 to reduce the desired gap bound to a zero-sum estimate.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the prime-side combinatorial core of Theorem 2 before the frequency split.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The interval-containment argument is prose-recoverable; the exact normalization and target inequality are formula-sensitive and need scan checking.

accepted_units.title: Bound low zero frequencies through partial summation and pair-correlation energy
accepted_units.why_material: Handles the low-ordinate portion of the zero sum by crude weight bounds, partial summation, Cauchy-Schwarz, and Lemma 3, producing a pair-correlation bound at the short-interval scale.
accepted_units.context_note: Represents one half of the proof's frequency decomposition and shows when the exact L2 identity suffices directly.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependency; the move sequence and low-frequency role are clear, but exact weights and constants require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Control high zero frequencies by scale decomposition
accepted_units.why_material: Rewrites the high-frequency weight as a difference of scaled factors, applies partial summation and Cauchy-Schwarz, and integrates the resulting energies to obtain a maximum over pair-correlation scales, completing Theorem 2.
accepted_units.context_note: Complements the low-frequency unit and explains why the theorem's hypothesis ranges over a family of scales rather than one point.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High; formulas are substantially degraded, so only the checked strategic decomposition is safe without the scan.

accepted_units.title: Express a weighted zero-sum energy through pair correlation
accepted_units.why_material: Expands a weighted exponential-sum energy into pairs of zeros, replaces asymmetric weights with a controlled symmetric form, and uses partial summation to rewrite the result as a transform of the pair-correlation function.
accepted_units.context_note: This prepares a sharper, sign-sensitive relation for Theorem 3 beyond the upper bounds used in Theorem 2.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependency; the expansion, symmetry correction, and transform role are recoverable, but exact kernels and errors need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Truncate the energy integral and isolate the Lemma 5 kernel
accepted_units.why_material: Obtains a uniform global energy bound, chooses a logarithmic cutoff to suppress tails, and differentiates the weight into a kernel that yields Lemma 5 with a controlled error.
accepted_units.context_note: Supplies the admissible bounded window and kernel identity consumed immediately in the final proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High; cutoff logic is prose-supported, while the precise kernel and powers require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Combine prime variance and zero energy after a logarithmic change of variables
accepted_units.why_material: Aligns Lemmas 2 and 5 by an exponential change of variables and a sum over translated windows, converting the smoothed prime-counting variance into an integral of pair correlation against a derived kernel.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the principal synthesis step inside the carried full proof unit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High; variable substitutions and the error summation are OCR-sensitive and require scan verification for exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Average the interval scale to localize the pair-correlation hypothesis
accepted_units.why_material: Introduces a compact triangular average in the short-interval parameter, thereby restricting the transform to the theorem's usable pair-correlation range and separating the main term from endpoint and hypothesis errors.
accepted_units.context_note: Explains why an auxiliary average is structurally necessary rather than cosmetic.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high formula dependency; the averaging purpose and range localization are clear, but the kernel evaluation needs scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Extract a close prime pair from diagonal and off-diagonal mass
accepted_units.why_material: Uses continuity to choose a good scale, expands the nonnegative variance into background, linear, and prime-pair terms, evaluates the diagonal, bounds remote off-diagonal ranges by the sieve estimate, and forces positive mass from nearby distinct primes.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the final existence mechanism and is reusable as an energy-to-witness pattern.
